grammar.title: Relative clause: who, which, whose
grammar.explanation: Relative clause menambahkan keterangan pada kata benda. Tanpa koma (defining) berarti informasinya penting untuk menentukan yang dimaksud. Dengan koma (non-defining) berarti informasi tambahan, dan di sini tidak boleh memakai 'that'. 'Whose' menyatakan kepemilikan.
examples: Engineers who use AI tools save time.
The report, which was published last week, surprised many experts.
Workers whose jobs are at risk need retraining.

common_mistake.wrong: The study, that was published in 2023, was widely shared.
common_mistake.right: The study, which was published in 2023, was widely shared.

grammar.title: Although, despite, whereas
grammar.explanation: 'Although' diikuti klausa lengkap (subjek + kata kerja). 'Despite' diikuti kata benda atau V-ing, bukan klausa. 'Whereas' membandingkan dua hal yang berbeda.
examples: Although AI is powerful, it still makes mistakes.
Despite the risks, many companies use it.
Some jobs will disappear, whereas others will be created.

common_mistake.wrong: Despite AI is powerful, it makes mistakes.
common_mistake.right: Although AI is powerful, it makes mistakes.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Welcome back. Today we're asking a big question: will AI replace our jobs?

lines.speaker: Dr Okafor
lines.text: It's a fair question. Automation has always replaced some tasks, but it rarely replaces whole jobs overnight.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: So which workers should be worried?

lines.speaker: Dr Okafor
lines.text: People whose work is mostly routine, like data entry, face the highest risk.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: And what about creative jobs, such as design?

lines.speaker: Dr Okafor
lines.text: Although AI can produce images quickly, clients still rely on designers to understand what they actually need.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: So the key is to keep up with the tools rather than fight them?

lines.speaker: Dr Okafor
lines.text: Exactly. A growing number of companies are hiring people who can work with AI, not against it.

questions.q: According to Dr Okafor, what does automation usually replace?

questions.explain: 'Keep up with the tools' = mengikuti perkembangan alat, bukan melawannya.

reading.title: Can AI make us lazy thinkers?
reading.text: A growing number of studies are looking at how AI assistants affect the way we think. In one experiment carried out at a European university, two groups of students wrote short essays. The first group could use an AI tool, whereas the second group could only use a search engine. The essays written with AI were finished faster and contained fewer grammar mistakes. However, when the students were tested a week later, those who had relied on AI remembered significantly less of what they had written. The researchers call this 'cognitive offloading': when a tool does the thinking for us, our brains invest less effort in storing the information. This does not mean AI should be avoided. It could be argued that calculators caused similar fears decades ago. The lesson is to use AI as a coach that asks questions, not as a ghostwriter that answers them.

questions.q: What was the difference between the two groups?
options: One group used AI, the other used a search engine
AI should be banned in schools
AI should be used to ask questions, not to do the work
Calculators are more dangerous than AI

writing.prompt: IELTS Writing Task 2 (lengkap): 'Some people believe that artificial intelligence will create more jobs than it destroys. Others think it will lead to widespread unemployment. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.' Tulis esai 4 paragraf: pendahuluan, pandangan pertama, pandangan kedua, dan kesimpulan berisi pendapatmu.
checklist: Pendahuluan memparafrasekan soal dan menyebut pendapatmu
Satu paragraf untuk tiap pandangan, masing-masing dengan contoh
Penghubung kontras (Although / Whereas / On the other hand)
Minimal satu relative clause (which / who / whose)
Kesimpulan menegaskan pendapat tanpa ide baru
useful_phrases: While some argue that ..., others fear that ...
writing.model_answer:
Artificial intelligence is developing so quickly that many people are worried about the future of work. While some argue that AI will generate more jobs than it eliminates, others fear that it will leave millions unemployed. In my view, both outcomes are possible, but the result will depend on how well societies prepare.

On the one hand, history suggests that new technology tends to create new kinds of work. When computers became widespread, typists disappeared, but millions of jobs were created in software, design and online services. Similarly, AI is already producing roles such as data annotators and AI trainers, which did not exist ten years ago. Companies that use AI to become more productive may also grow and hire more staff.

On the other hand, the speed of this change is unusual. Workers whose tasks are mostly routine, like customer service agents or data entry clerks, could lose their jobs faster than they can retrain. Although new positions may appear, they often require skills that these workers do not have, and they may be located in different cities or even countries. Without support, this could lead to serious inequality.

In conclusion, I believe AI is more likely to change jobs than to destroy work altogether. However, governments and employers must tackle the transition seriously by investing in affordable training, so that the benefits of automation are shared widely rather than concentrated in the hands of a few.

sentences: It could be argued that AI makes workers more productive.
Social media is a double-edged sword for young people.
Although AI is powerful, it still makes mistakes.
Workers whose jobs are at risk need retraining.
It's hard to keep up with new tools every month.
speaking.focus: Linking 'could be argued' (could-be-AR-gued), 'double-edged' dengan bunyi /dʒd/ di akhir, dan bunyi /ð/ pada 'although'.

speaking.prompt: IELTS Speaking Part 2: 'Describe a piece of technology you use every day.' Sebutkan apa itu, bagaimana kamu memakainya, dan kenapa penting bagimu. Bicara 1 sampai 2 menit (6 sampai 8 kalimat).
speaking.sample_answer: The piece of technology I couldn't live without is my laptop. I use it for almost everything: coding at work, studying English in the evening, and even watching films at the weekend. I bought it about two years ago, when my old one became too slow to run modern development tools. What I like most is that it's light enough to carry around, so I can work from a café when I need a change of scene. Having said that, it's a double-edged sword, because it also makes it very hard to switch off from work. I've started closing it completely after eight in the evening to protect my free time. Overall, it's the tool that has helped my career the most, and I'd probably feel lost without it.

conversation.title: Debat santai: AI di tempat kerja

n1.them: Did you see the email? Management wants everyone to use AI coding tools from next month. I'm not a fan.

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "Really? Why not? I think they could save us a lot of time."

n2.them: Because people will stop thinking. If the tool writes the code, how will juniors learn?
hints: akui sebagian: That's a fair point, but ...

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "That's a fair point, but juniors could still learn if they review the code instead of just copying it."

n3.them: Maybe. But there's also the security risk. Our code would be sent to an external company.

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "We could use a tool that runs locally, or only use it for code that isn't sensitive."

n4.them: Okay, that would help. So what would you suggest we tell management?
hints: usulan konkret: Why don't we suggest ...?
uji coba kecil dengan aturan jelas

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "Why don't we suggest a one-month pilot with clear guidelines, and then review the results?"

end.them: Good idea. Let's write it up together and send it this afternoon.
